comparisons.peer_summary: AMD entered an agreement in August 2024 to acquire ZT Systems, expected to close in the first half of fiscal year 2025, to enhance data center AI rack and infrastructure capabilities; AMD also intends to seek a strategic partner for ZT's manufacturing business.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose a strategy of pursuing acquisitions to complement strategic objectives and strengthen core capabilities, though AMD specifies its acquisition of ZT Systems to enhance AI infrastructure while Intel states a general opportunistic approach. Intel states: 'Our capital allocation strategy also includes opportunistic investment in and acquisition of companies that complement our strategic objectives.' AMD states: 'We also focused on building our data center AI rack and data center-scale solutions capabilities by entering into an agreement to acquire ZT Group Int'l, Inc. (ZT Systems)... We believe that with the acquisition of ZT Systems, we can deliver leadership training and inferencing solutions that can accelerate time to deployment for our AMD Instinct platforms.'

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD completed the acquisition of Silo AI in 2024, expanding its AI model development capabilities and gaining a software stack for training large language models on AMD Instinct accelerators.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and AMD both utilize acquisitions to supplement and expand their R&D and technical capabilities. Intel highlights acquisitions that 'supplement and strengthen our capital and R&D investments,' while AMD details the acquisition of Silo AI to 'expanded our capability to accelerate development and deployment of AI models on AMD hardware,' specifically gaining expertise in software stacks for AI training. Intel states: 'We look for acquisitions that supplement and strengthen our capital and R&D investments.' AMD states: 'The acquisition of Silo AI expanded our capability to accelerate development and deployment of AI models on AMD hardware.'
